name: Kabixí
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. Change Request 2015-026 (submitted 2015-04-28 by the Editor, Ethnologue; effective 2016-01-15): retire xbx Kabixí.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not a linguistic description. Rationale p.2: 'There is much confusion about the existence of the Cabixi/Kabixi language [xbx]. Loukotka (1968) lists Cabixi as an unknown or unclassified language in Mato Grosso.. and Kabixi as a Chapacuran language spoken in Rondonia.. Campbell (1997) also lists Kabishi (Kabixi) as a Chapacuran language (p.178) as well as a Nambiquaran language.. Price (1983) shows.. that Kabixi (Cabixi) was a generic term used for any hostile group, both for the Parecis as well as for the Nambiquaran groups.. Because it is unclear as to which language(s) Kabixi (Cabixi) actua…

sources.citation: Angenot-de Lima, Geralda. 1997. Fonotática e fonologia do lexema Protochapakura. Dissertação de Mestrado, Universidade Federal de Rondônia (Guajará-Mirim). 177 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Held under wany1246 (Wanyam), where it is the statement of record (weight-sensitive: 'Nas línguas Chapakura, a acentuação dos lexemas é dedutível do peso silábico.. uma sílaba pesada é tônica e possui um tom alto', p.24), with Miguelenho-Wanham data from the last speaker. Its language list (line 536 ff.) names 'Kabishi-Wañam' (r. Manoel Correia / r. Preto -> r. São Miguel; c.1950 5 speakers per Wanda Hanke; 83 words + 16 song lines by Hanke) as a Wanyam variety, i.e. the only 'Kabixi' with linguistic data is a Wanyam dialect. Not re-quoted here because it belongs to key wany1246.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page kabi1264 'Kabixí' and reference record 22476 (Hasemann 1912), accessed 2026-09-17; Glottolog name searches for 'Kabixi' and 'Pawumwa'.
sources.note: Languoid is retired/bookkeeping ('based on a misunderstanding to begin with'); ref 22476 is the only reference linked, typed grammar sketch by computerized assignment from 'notes', provider Fabre's Diccionario etnolingüístico; family shown as Chapacura-Wanham. Name search: 'Kabixi' resolves to Parecís (pare1272, Arawakan); 'Pawumwa' resolves to Wanyam (wany1246, Chapacuran).

sources.citation: Birchall, Joshua, Michael Dunn & Simon Greenhill. 2016. A combined comparative and phylogenetic analysis of the Chapacuran language family. IJAL 82(3): 255-284.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Seen via the wany1246 check record: pp.258-259 equate Wanyam = Pawumwa (Haseman 1912), Miguelenho (Ribeiro 1998), Cabixi (Hanke 1975, 'nearly identical to the Miguelenho dialect'); silent on stress.

sources.citation: Price, David. 1983. Pareci, Cabixi, Nambiquara: a case study in the western classification of native peoples. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 69: 129-148.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Identity only: the ethnohistorical analysis (cited by the ISO retirement request) showing 'Cabixi' was a generic term for hostile groups applied to Paresi and Nambikwara; needed if anyone wants to map old 'Kabixi' wordlists to real glottocodes. No stress content expected.

sources.citation: Chamberlain, Alexander F. 1912. The linguistic position of the Pawumwa Indians of South America. American Anthropologist n.s. 14(4): 632-635. DOI 10.1525/aa.1912.14.4.02a00060.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lexical comparison of Haseman's vocabulary with d'Orbigny's Ite and Chapacura lists; groups Pawumwa with Chapacura and Ite ('Pawumwan'); p.635 identifies Haseman's kabi'ci 'bad man, enemy' with the name Kabixi of an Arawakan tribe living with the Paressi at the sources of the Cabaçal, Jauru, Juruena and Guaporé. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Haseman, J. D. 1912. Some notes on the Pawumwa Indians of South America. American Anthropologist n.s. 14(2): 333-349. DOI 10.1525/aa.1912.14.2.02a00080. (Glottolog ref 22476, the only reference linked to kabi1264.)

sources.note: Ethnographic notes on the Pawumwa of the Rio Guaporé/Rio São Miguel (Rondônia) with a 123-word vocabulary pp.347-349 whose spelling was revised by R. H. Lowie from Haseman's recollection. The phonetic key (p.347) defines only segmental symbols and nasalization ('Vowels have their continental values: n indicates nasalization; tc represents ch.; c the sound of English sh.; j French j'); the words carry an accent tick after a vowel (itopi', katu'wa, iparama'tci, tu'kitci, i'ritci, pana', kim, ika't) that is never explained; the only prosodic remark is 'ki'na'm, jaguar (the second syllable with r…
